about: The MongoDB the game servers keep their worlds in (#6237). scripts/deploy/Install-Mongo.ps1 installs these three downloads on the box, each checked against its SHA-256 before it is used, runs mongod as the task Thornswood Mongo on loopback only with authorization on, and makes one user per server, a backup user and an admin. MongoDB's own download records give each SHA-256 (downloads.mongodb.org/full.json, downloads.mongodb.org/tools/db/release.json, downloads.mongodb.com/compass/mongosh.json), and each was checked against the file on 16 Nov 2026. The engine's driver (the fork's mongo-c-driver 2.2.3) is held to the 8.0 series. Community Server, Database Tools and mongosh are free; nothing here is paid. Nothing here is secret: the passwords are made on the box and kept there.
cacheWhy: The box has 8 GB and runs two game servers (about 1 GB each under 100 people, #4623), two voice services, the site and the bot. MongoDB's default cache is half of the memory less 1 GB, 3.5 GB here. A 20,000-form world is 55 MB of JSON, so half a gigabyte holds every world several times over; the load test (#6237) says whether it is enough.

load.why: The load test's copy of a server whose world is in MongoDB (Load-Box.ps1) keeps its bots' characters here, never in a server's own database, so the test measures saves the way the server makes them. Emptied before and after each run. Only SYSTEM and Administrators read its file: the load test runs from the deploy gate.

rehearsal.why: The monthly restore rehearsal (Rehearse-OnBox.ps1) puts a backup's world here, never into a server's own database, starts a server on it and empties it again. Only SYSTEM and Administrators read its file: the rehearsal runs from the deploy gate.
